newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sun, then rain in key Brazil soybean regions - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Sun, then rain in key Brazil soybean regions - Somar.

text.p: Sunshine will prevail at the start of the week in Brazil's key southern soybean growing regions but a cold front will bring scattered rains later in the week, forecast independent meteorologists Somar.
In the southeast and centersouth, the week is expected to start rainy and humid. Rains will diminish in the centersouth by December 25 although in Mato Grosso late afternoon showers will remain.
A cold front is seen heading south on December 26th and 27th but will weaken before reaching the southeast, Somar predicted.

A second cold front was expected to hit the key growing region of Rio Grande do Sul on December 28, bringing with it heavy rains. Meanwhile, the southeast and centerwest will see isolated late afternoon showers.
Somar said that last week's rains had increased soil moisture levels at a crucial point in the development of the soybean.
Rainfall was irregular in Rio Grande do Sul with Santa Maria registering 118 mm and other areas not exceeding 40 mm.
Parana state also benefited from rainfall after a period of dryness. In Mato Grosso, isolated rains were within the average for the period.
